title: Echo Briefcase — Customer Synthesis & Request Ledger
content:
Purpose:
This is a working synthesis of recent customer conversations (May–Jul 2026) focused on runtime availability, cost predictability, and request-level controls. Goal is to convert raw field notes into a compact ledger we can hand to Product + Eng for prioritization and to PMM for messaging.

TL;DR (one paragraph):
Customers repeatedly surface three clusters: (A) need stronger per-route controls (pin model versions, per-route rate/cost caps, clearer fallback behavior), (B) hotspots around latency variability and KV/prefix caching behavior in multi-tenant scenarios, and (C) cost transparency and tooling — suggestions for token-level cost breakdowns, predicted cost per burst, and simulated billing for canary runs. A set of 7 quick wins and 5 medium-term proposals below.

How I compiled this (method):
- Sources: 23 post-demo follow-ups, 11 support threads, 9 onboarding interviews, and notes from two CSM quarterly reviews.
- Timestamp window: 2026-05-01 to 2026-07-10.
- Heuristic: quoted asks verbatim where possible; clustered by customer impact (frequency x severity).

Representative raw signals (verbatim snippets):
- “We had a canary flip that re-routed to a quantized model — cost dropped 40% but hallucinations doubled. We need predictable fallback rules.” — fintech customer
- “When we enable prefix cache on multi-tenant dedicated pools, throughput is fine but tail latency spikes for some customers.” — platform partner
- “Show me estimated cost before a 50k message burst; don’t make me guess.” — mid-market SaaS
- “Pinning model + tokenizer together would save us from subtle drift during rollouts.” — health-tech compliance lead
- “We need per-route SLA that guarantees latency percentiles, not best effort.” — enterprise content moderation team

Clusters and synthesized asks (ranked):
1) Route-level controls & rollout determinism (HIGH frequency, HIGH severity)
   - Asks: per-route model pinning (model+tokenizer+quantization), explicit fallback chains (e.g., route X -> model A else B, with telemetry flags when fallback triggers), per-route cost caps and throttles.
   - Example customer value: prevents canary surprises and regulatory drift during rollouts.
   - Proposed impact metric: reduce rollback frequency by % (baseline TBD), fewer incidents where hallucination regressions reach production.

2) Caching + KV behavior in shared/dedicated pools (MED frequency, HIGH severity for some)
   - Asks: visibility into KV cache hit/miss per route, controls for prefix cache TTL and eviction priority, isolation knobs in dedicated pools so single-tenant heavy prefixes don't degrade others.
   - Customer pain: unpredictable tail latency and throttled throughput on multi-tenant Dedicated nodes.
   - Quick monitoring idea: per-route moving average of KV-hit-rate + 95th latency annotated in Console.

3) Cost transparency and simulation tools (HIGH frequency, MED severity)
   - Asks: predicted spend for burst/rollout, token-level breakdown per model variant, ability to simulate cost given a prompt set and expected QPS.
   - Workaround customers use: local heuristics and staging meter runs — brittle and hard to standardize.
   - PMM note: would be excellent for PLG onboarding (convert trial -> committed capacity).

4) Observability and tracing for inference stack (MED frequency, MED severity)
   - Asks: lighten instrumentation for high-volume clients (sampling rules), correlate client token IDs to traces without leaking PII, add per-request quality regression flags (when reranking or cached prefixes change output).

5) Ops ergonomics for Dedicated & Private (LOW frequency, HIGH severity for enterprise)
   - Asks: smoother autoscale feedback loop, deterministic cold-start behavior, clearer on-prem upgrade notes, improved KMS rotation guidance.

Suggested quick wins (<= 2 sprints):
- Console: show per-route fallback counter and last fallback timestamp (low-risk UI + telemetry). Owner: Console PM + CS spike.
- Billing UI: add “simulate burst” microflow: let user enter QPS+payload size -> show estimated spend for 1h/24h. Owner: Billing PM.
- Instrument KV cache visibility: add per-route KV hit ratio metric (no perf changes). Owner: Observability eng.
- Run a small canary playbook with a handful of high-usage customers to collect failure modes when rolling model variants; produce a short playbook for CS/SEs. Owner: Solutions Eng.
- Add an example in docs: how to pin model+tokenizer+quantization in a rollout config (docs + snippet). Owner: DevEx.

Medium-term proposals (3–6 months):
- Per-route deterministic rollouts: allow explicit fallback chains and per-route model pin metadata; release with telemetry and rollback TTL.
- Per-route cost caps + throttling policy: server-enforced soft caps with alerting and hard throttles as a safety net.
- Dedicated pool isolation knobs: tenant-reservations and eviction-priority settings to avoid noisy-neighbor tail spikes.
- Cost simulation API (server-side): accept a prompt set + expected QPS -> return estimated tokens, compute cost across model variants. Useful for sales + PLG.

Longer bets (6–12 months):
- Predictive cost engine that integrates KV caching and batching effects to recommend model variant + batching config for a target latency and budget.
- Per-route SLOs with automated fallback to cheaper model within latency/SLA constraints.

Customer quotes mapped to asks (short list):
- FintechCorp — pinned model + explicit fallback chain (asks 1 + 3).
- HealthCo — model+tokenizer pinning and audit trail for rollout (asks 1 + 5).
- MarketBot — KV visibility and eviction controls (ask 2).
- ShopFlow — simulate bursts in Console and billing preview (ask 3).

Risk assessment / engineering cost band (very rough):
- UI-only telemetry additions (low cost)
- Console billing-simulation + API (medium cost: 2–3 sprints + billing infra work)
- Deterministic fallback + per-route caps (higher cost: changes in routing and policy engine; ~2–3 months)
- Predictive cost engine (high research + infra cost; research spike required)

Operational playbook (for CS + SEs):
- For incoming tickets that mention “unexpected fallback” -> tag as rollback-risk, capture last-fallback timestamp, and proactively offer to pin model during canary window.
- For latency complaints: collect KV-hit-rate, batch size distribution, and last deploy id; open ENG ticket with reproducible QPS window.

Next steps & owners (immediate):
- Maya P (owner): run short audit across top-10 ARR customers to validate frequency of rollback incidents (due 2026-07-30).
- Jonas K (solutions): draft canary playbook template and run two live canaries with consenting customers (due 2026-08-20).
- Priya R (observability): prototype KV-hit-rate metric in Console (due 2026-08-10).
- Billing PM: assess feasibility of a 1-click burst simulation (ask for 2-sprint estimate).

Open questions / unresolved threads (notes to self):
- How tightly coupled must tokenizer pinning be to runtime deploy metadata? (Consequence of mismatch is subtle: scoring drift.)
- Is hard per-route throttling acceptable for enterprise SLAs, or will customers prefer soft alerts + manual throttles?
- Data retention & privacy: how do we expose per-route traces without PII risk? Need Security + Legal review.

Appendix: checklist for the canary playbook (working draft)
- Obtain explicit sign-off from customer that they accept potential quality regressions.
- Define traffic percentage and rollback threshold.
- Configure telemetry: fallback counter, KV-hit-rate, 95th latency.
- Pre-capture baseline outputs on a representative prompt set (store hashed prompts).
- Post-canary: run quality regression checks and summarize cost delta.

Notes / loose ideas (brainstorm fragments):
- Could we expose a “what-if” CSV export for customers to run offline cost experiments?
- Small UX experiment: when a fallback occurs, surface a non-intrusive toast to the operator that links to the last-three prompts (hashed) that triggered fallback.
- Consider metadata tags for model variants that indicate "safety sensitivity" so fallbacks prefer safer models for regulated customers.

If you read only one thing: run the top-10 ARR audit (owner: Maya) and prototype per-route KV-hit metric (owner: Priya). Those two pieces will validate frequency and give a cheap instrumentation win to show customers.
